text: {"claims":[{"cid":"c1","text":"Two doses of a measles-containing vaccine give about 97 percent protection against measles infection in controlled effectiveness studies.","cited_pids":["vaccines_measles#0"]},{"cid":"c2","text":"Serological studies show neutralising antibodies persist for decades after the standard two-dose measles vaccine schedule.","cited_pids":["vaccines_measles#3"]},{"cid":"c3","text":"National measles incidence fell by more than 99 percent after routine childhood vaccination was introduced.","cited_pids":["vaccines_measles#1"]},{"cid":"c4","text":"Measles outbreaks concentrate among unvaccinated people.","cited_pids":["vaccines_measles#2"]},{"cid":"c5","text":"Measles resurgence follows declines in vaccination coverage.","cited_pids":["vaccines_measles#7"]},{"cid":"c6","text":"Post-exposure measles vaccination within 72 hours reduces the probability of clinical disease.","cited_pids":["vaccines_measles#6"]},{"cid":"c7","text":"The passages do not address measles vaccine failure rates in detail beyond the roughly 97 percent figure.","cited_pids":[]}]}
